question: Can the physical witness bind each held child to the actual S1 file descriptor without trusting caller-supplied /proc fd rows?

primary_sources.claim: pidfd_getfd duplicates targetfd from the process referenced by pidfd and the duplicate refers to the same open file description; permission is subject to PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH_REALCREDS; Linux history begins at 5.6.
pidfd_open creates a stable descriptor referring to a task and pidfd_getfd is an intended use of that process handle.
F_GETFL returns access mode/status flags associated with the open file description and duplicated descriptors share those flags.
proc fdinfo exposes fd flags and mount identity but is still a separately read observation surface rather than a duplicated target descriptor.

finding.mechanism: During the live held barrier, open one pidfd per child, then use pidfd_getfd(pidfd, observed_target_fd, 0) inside the mint authority boundary. fstat the duplicated descriptor and F_GETFL it locally, and compare device+inode/access-mode against the canonical S1 path stat performed inside the same boundary.
finding.why_stronger_than_caller_fd_rows: The mint authority obtains a duplicate of the actual descriptor owned by the process incarnation referenced by pidfd. Caller-provided fdinfo rows are no longer sufficient to create the claimed S1 binding.
remaining_nonproofs: A valid pidfd plus duplicated S1 descriptor does not by itself prove the child currently holds the intended SQLite read transaction.
It does not bind the later NODE_RESULT/read-receipt/snapshot packet unless a pre-release commitment is produced and checked after release.
It does not prove observer source-byte consumption identity by itself.

recommended_fusion: Acquire pidfds before release/reap in the retained held-cohort lifecycle.

Inside the same mint boundary, stat the canonical S1 path and duplicate each child's observed S1 target fd with pidfd_getfd; locally fstat and F_GETFL the duplicate; reject device/inode or access-mode mismatch.
Bind each pidfd/process incarnation, duplicated-S1 identity, ready marker, generation/epoch/state digest and pre-release NODE_RESULT or packet commitment into one immutable physical witness.
After release, require the final packet/read-receipt to match the pre-release commitment before the sole FusedFabric mutation path is reachable.
Make raw proof mappings unreachable from every public PHYSICAL_OBSERVED commit entry; retain a distinct SOURCE_FIXTURE_ONLY route with hard zero physical/model/training credit.
Fail closed with an explicit UNSUPPORTED_PIDFD_GETFD_OR_PTRACE_POLICY code when kernel/syscall/permission support is unavailable; do not silently fall back to caller-supplied physical evidence.
counterhypothesis: Reading /proc/<pid>/fdinfo plus statting /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> inside the boundary is sufficient and simpler.
counterhypothesis_adjudication: It can be a bounded compatibility fallback only if its race/provenance semantics are explicitly accepted and tested. pidfd_getfd is the higher-information Linux-specific discriminator because the returned descriptor is tied to the pidfd-referenced process and the same open file description. No fallback may upgrade caller-supplied fd rows into physical evidence.
preconditions_and_failure_modes: Linux kernel must support pidfd_getfd (documented since Linux 5.6).
The process must satisfy the ptrace access check PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH_REALCREDS; EPERM is an infrastructure/capability result, not a scientific negative.
Python may require a direct syscall/ctypes wrapper because a high-level stdlib pidfd_getfd wrapper is not assumed here.
All duplicated descriptors must be closed on success and failure paths.
No execution credit is granted until exact-current admitted runtime proves the path.
next_exact_action: Re-enter moving main. If the single retained physical witness path is still open, fuse live-barrier pidfd acquisition plus pidfd_getfd-derived actual S1 descriptor binding and a pre-release packet commitment into that sole path; keep raw dictionaries and SOURCE_FIXTURE_ONLY structurally disjoint.
